the elastic scattering amplitude can be separated into a diffractive and a refractive part.
the refractive and the diffractive parts are not independent and, therefore, cannot be added in the usual way.
the refractive and diffraction parts of the elastic angular distributions of heavy ions at energies around the Coulomb barrier can be separated and analyzed independently.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a good representation of the elastic scattering data can be obtained without invoking a diffractive phase, which is a very important result, since it shows that the refractive part alone is sufficient to explain the data, and that the diffractive phase does not play any significant role in the description of the scattering data.

the interference between refraction and diffraction is not negligible, even in the region of the rainbow angle, and that it is not possible to fit data with the usual model, which assumes that the refraction and diffractions are additive.

the diffractive part of the elastic scattering amplitudes is much larger than that of the refractive part, which implies that the interference between the refractive and the diffractive parts is negligible.
